the game's executable keeps this type name among its ECS type names (gatekit symbols types), as struct eoc::GameObjectVisualComponent, and in the queries of the client's equipment visuals

on Astarion in Basic_Level_A RootTemplateId reads his own template id, RootTemplateType 1, Scale 1.0, Type 0, Icon a name ending in his origin icon; the definition of a change-appearance session on him names another RootTemplate, the body's race template
reported from a run of character creation, not read again here: on the created character RootTemplateId equals the definition's RootTemplate, which follows race, subrace and body type

survey.names: Every name here is Script Extender's author's (his headers), not the game's own: they are kept because they are what the extender's Lua answers to and what bg3_verify compares, and every field carries the rung `extender` - the extender's name for the field at that offset, which nobody has checked against the game's code. A name is raised from `extender` only with evidence from the code, by `gatekit names set`.
